extracted.intended_audience: editors of Current Contents and authors of highly-cited papers invited to contribute Citation Classics commentaries
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and editorial policy for producing short retrospective 'Citation Classics' commentaries for Current Contents: who to invite, what content and tone are required, how selections are distributed across editions, and scheduling/production targets. Emphasizes disciplinary representation and practical publication procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual production volume target
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish roughly 250 to 300 unique commentaries in print per year (in 1979 the goal was to publish 250 to 300 unique commentaries to reduce backlog).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This expansion allows getting manuscripts into print faster and reduces backlog of invited authors waiting to see their commentaries published.

rubrics_metrics.name: One Citation Classic per Current Contents edition
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Current Contents edition will contain a Citation Classic appropriate to that edition; the six CC editions will each present classics so that over the year all fields are covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scheduling Classics across the six different editions ensures that all fields are adequately represented over the course of the year; a page of CC will list the classics appearing in each of the six editions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection pool: invite authors of most-cited papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors of the most-cited papers (e.g., the 300–500 most-cited papers identified in prior studies) are invited to submit commentaries on their works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the series began (1977) authors of the 500 most-cited papers were asked to submit; invitations and solicitation are central to sourcing commentaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commentary content: focus on the human side and reasons for impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are asked to discuss the human side of scientific reports — the roles they and co-authors played, the sequence of events, and to explain why their papers have such high impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commentaries should illuminate personal, historical, and sociological aspects of the work as well as the technical reasons for citation impact; this 'human side' dimension is a primary purpose of the series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commentary style and length: short, retrospective, personal reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Commentaries are expected to be short, personal, retrospective reports rather than long formal papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The brief, personal format allows authors to give anecdotal and retrospective perspective; co-authors may contribute accounts of technical evolution and the history of the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely solely on absolute citation counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Absolute citation counts should not be the exclusive criterion for selecting classics because citation frequencies vary widely between disciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors recognize that some disciplines are 'naturally' higher in citation counts; selection must account for disciplinary differences so important works in low-citation fields are not excluded merely due to lower absolute counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure disciplinary diversity and adequate representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection should ensure adequate representation across fields (physical & chemical sciences, life sciences, clinical practice, social & behavioral sciences, statistics, agriculture, engineering, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Past selections showed preponderance from life sciences; editorial policy adjusts selection to include papers from underrepresented disciplines and to present a balanced list in figures and listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow and solicit commentary from co-authors and on technical evolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Co-authors may be invited or allowed to write commentaries that include discussion of technical developments and evolution related to the cited work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encouraging co-authors to discuss technical evolution broadens coverage of the work's development and subsequent impact; the editorial approach explicitly invites such perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial procedure for invitations and backlog management
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors will invite authors, maintain a backlog of invited commentaries, apologize to those waiting, and plan mid-year summaries of progress; many invited authors do respond and submit over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of backlog and variable author response (some authors deceased or unable to respond), active solicitation and periodic summaries are used to manage production and inform readers of progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation and metadata: arrange classics by journal and category with full citation details
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists/figures of Citation Classics should be arranged by journal and by category, providing full bibliographic citation (title, authors, journal, year) under each category heading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizing classics by journal and topical category helps readers navigate the list and see disciplinary grouping; examples are provided in the figures showing detailed citation entries.
